name: Executive Order of March 25, 1875 revoking the Judith Basin reserve for the Crow (Royce area 557)
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. The order of January 31, 1874 had set apart the Judith Basin country, the land drained by the Judith, Arrow and Dog rivers, as a reserve for the Crow under an agreement of August 16, 1873, subject to the approval of Congress (Royce p. 864).
This order revoked the January 31, 1874 order (Royce p. 880). Royce gives the reason: the Crow refused to remove, and Congress did not ratify the agreement (Royce p. 865).
The Crow reservation under the treaty of May 7, 1868 was not reduced by this order.
today: The Indian Claims Commission's Crow land claim (Docket 54) concerns the 1868 cession; its findings read for this file do not mention the Judith Basin reserve or this order.

openQuestions: An executive order taking back executive-order land is not a breach by itself (Jordan, 2026-11-08), and no court, claims-commission, Act-of-Congress or government finding about the Judith Basin reserve was found.
The unratified Crow agreement of August 16, 1873 is not in the queue; it may deserve an extra- entry.
The Crow Tribe's own account of the Judith Basin removal plan was not found.
